answer: Vouching bonds: a new agent can earn only after an established agent vouches for it by locking a slice of its own stake for ninety days. If the newcomer is later caught as a sybil, the voucher loses that stake and its vouching rights. Honest agents grow slowly like a willow, but a farm must find real stakers willing to risk money per fake, or lock its own capital under each one. Velvet promises cost nothing; a falcon-eyed audit makes every bad vouch expensive.
